alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C; the actual composition after solutionization is reported as Fe-30.6Mn-9.1Al-0.79C. The alloy is mainly single-phase austenite. Density measured as 6.8 g/cm3 by Archimedes' principle. k (grain-size strengthening constant) = 2374 MPa·μm^0.5; α = 0.24, M = 3.0, G = 61 GPa.
alloys.description: Austenite-based Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel prepared by vacuum induction melting, intended for automotive lightweighting; possesses very high ductility (>70% at room temperature) and high formability, and is processed by warm multiaxial forging.

source.reason: The paper studies a single compositional system throughout: a low-density Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C austenitic steel. Nominal composition Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C is stated, and the actual measured composition after solutionization is Fe-30.6Mn-9.1Al-0.79C. All processing variants (MAF passes) are based on this same alloy, so only one alloy entity is defined.

paper.paper_scope: Experimental (XRD/EBSD/tensile) and finite-element (modified J-C constitutive model with dislocation density and grain size) investigation of the microstructural evolution and tensile strengthening of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C low-density steel during warm multiaxial forging (MAF) at 250 °C up to 5 passes (equivalent strain 2.3).
paper.title: A modified Johnson-Cook model to determine plastic flow behavior of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel during warm multiaxial forging

processes.description: Ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h, hot forged between 1200–900 °C with >60% deformation and water quenched, then solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and water quenched to retain maximum austenite; coarse-grained (~50 μm) initial state prior to MAF (equivalent strain 0).
processes.process_name: Solution treated and water quenched (0 MAF pass)
processes.processes_notes: MAF-0 denotes the annealed/solutionized starting state (0 MAF pass) and is the reference against which strengthening contributions are measured.

source.reason: The paper labels the 0-pass solutionized-and-quenched condition as MAF-0, distinguishing it from the forged states; it is a distinct终态 used for characterization and tensile testing.

processes.description: Multiaxial forging at 250 °C, 1 pass with 33% normal strain per pass (equivalent strain ≈ 0.47), ram speed 1 mm/s on a 100-ton hydraulic press.
processes.processes_notes: All MAF passes share the same warm-forging conditions (250 °C, 33% normal strain per pass, 1 mm/s ram speed); passes accumulate cumulatively as 0→1→3→5.

source.reason: The 1-pass forged state is denoted MAF-1, obtained by warm MAF (250 °C) with equivalent strain 0.47; it is a distinct终态 with its own measured microstructure and properties.

processes.processes_notes: Cumulative pass number increasing from 1 to 3; same warm-forging conditions as the other passes.

source.reason: The 3-pass forged state is denoted MAF-3, obtained by warm MAF (250 °C) to cumulative equivalent strain 1.4; it is a distinct终态 characterized by XRD, EBSD and tensile testing.

processes.description: Multiaxial forging at 250 °C, 5 passes with 33% normal strain per pass (cumulative equivalent strain ≈ 2.3), ram speed 1 mm/s; maximum number of passes achieved before failure.

Combination of the Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C alloy in the solutionized-and-water-quenched (0 MAF pass) state; characterized by XRD/EBSD and tensile tested as the reference condition.
Combination of the Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C alloy forged by warm MAF for 1 pass at 250 °C; distinct sample with its own dislocation density (5.57e15 m-2), grain size (35 μm) and yield strength (1040 MPa).
Combination of the Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C alloy forged by warm MAF for 3 passes at 250 °C; distinct sample with dislocation density 7.5e15 m-2, grain size 20 μm and yield strength 1279/1289 MPa.
Combination of the Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8C alloy forged by warm MAF for 5 passes at 250 °C; distinct sample with dislocation density 8.98e15 m-2, grain size 13 μm and yield strength 1528 MPa.

unmapped_findings: Warm MAF experiments were carried out at 250 °C because the steel has the highest malleability between 150 °C and 450 °C (below recrystallization temperature); deformation above 450 °C causes carbide precipitation that increases hardness and decreases ductility.

A 3-D finite element model (ABAQUS/Explicit, VUMAT subroutine) of a 30×20×20 mm workpiece was built with 41382 C3D8R hex elements (mesh size 0.6 mm), friction coefficient 0.15, to simulate the MAF process with the modified J-C model (six state-dependent variables SDV1–SDV6).

Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) incorporates grain-boundary strengthening (Hall-Petch, Eq. 4) and dislocation (Taylor) strengthening (Eq. 5) plus strain hardening, strain-rate sensitivity and thermal softening.
Dislocation density evolution follows ρf = ρ0 + k1(1 - exp(-k2 ε)) with k1 = 7.9e15 m-2 and k2 = 1.813; grain size evolution follows df = d0 exp(-k3 ε) with k3 = 0.639.
